headline: Agents write the page, the kit gives them the parts, and the reader gets one HTML file to read, present and answer.
intro: v0.1 is the first cut of the artifact kit: a toolbox an agent uses to show what it did, found or proposes. The agent writes each page as TSX with the kit's components, the host adds an outline, present mode and a feedback drawer, and `artifact build` turns it into one self-contained HTML file. It grew over 13 rounds on Oct 12–13, each round driven by friction from real demo pages and by Alex's feedback.
shotsNote: Every `shot` path is `evidence/<file>.jpg`: copy screens/* into your artifact's evidence/ and the paths resolve. Screens are 1280 px wide JPEGs of the existing demos (http://mini.internal:5412/artifacts/<name>.html).

themes.title: Write the page
themes.oneLiner: An artifact is a directory: TSX (or MDX), data and evidence. The agent picks the structure.

themes.title: Read and present
themes.oneLiner: The host wraps every page with an outline, present mode, folding and a one-file download.

themes.title: Decide and give feedback
themes.oneLiner: Readers answer decisions on the page, leave comments, and copy it all back to the agent in one paste.

themes.title: Show the evidence
themes.oneLiner: Maps, real diffs, code with notes, time axes and step-by-step walks instead of prose.

themes.title: CLI and evidence
themes.oneLiner: new, dev, check, build, plus shot, capture and gather so agents can collect data and look at their own output.

themes.title: Multi-page
themes.oneLiner: Several pages in the same single HTML: hash routes, grouped nav, page cards and a tour.

rounds.summary: Kit, host chrome and CLI built; kit review fixed (evidence containment, check render filter, dev Host allowlist).
From the first demos' friction: Map fits its column, present-mode fixes, Scorecard, Actions, Facts, RiskMatrix, Gallery, DecisionIndex, `artifact shot`.
Gallery tiles, Stats, image lightbox, compact header, capture, gather, check advice.
JSX highlighting bug fixed, present mode on wide pages fixed, Timeline bucket/group/compact, gather --fields/--count.
For the investigation page: TimeAxis, usePresentSteps, shot --split.
Download, one Feedback drawer (comments + decisions), the decision walk (answerable Decision + When), Stages, Detail 1–4.
Detail 1–4 removed; sections fold on heading click; <More> replaces <Depth>.
Walkthrough; present-mode step sync for custom components; guide split into ARTIFACT.md + COMPONENTS.md.
Multi-page artifacts: pages as hash routes, grouped nav, PageCards, Link, prev/next, tour, feedback across pages.

features.title: Artifacts are directories the agent writes
features.oneLiner: `x.artifact/` holds artifact.json, index.tsx (or .mdx), data/*.json and evidence/. Kind is a free label; no shape is required.
features.why: Alex (Oct 12): the recap POC was too structured (fixed kinds, zoom levels 1–4, a block list). Ship a toolbox and let each artifact pick its own structure and flow.
features.how:
x.artifact/
  artifact.json   {"title","kind","audience","summary","sources":[...]}
  index.tsx       export default () => <Section title="Do first">…</Section>
  data/*.json     useData("prs")
  evidence/       *.patch *.replay images source files

features.title: Data and evidence inlined at build
features.oneLiner: `useData("name")` reads data/name.json; patches, replays, images and source files under evidence/ are inlined when cited, unused ones are left out.
features.why: The output is the thing people share, so it has to carry its own proof. The run-recap builder hit `evidence/${id}.jpg` failing check; template literals now act as a glob over evidence/.
features.how: const prs = useData("gh-prs"); // glob over evidence/

features.title: Status building blocks: Stats, Actions, Facts, PR, Ago
features.oneLiner: A stat row, a ranked do-first list with effort and recommendation, key/value facts, PR chips with conflict and age.
features.why: The status page builder wrote its own ActionQueue, Facts and useAgo; the canvas-run builder wrote its own Stats. Porting the status page to the kit removed 120 lines.
features.how:
<Stats items={[{ value: 1, label: "place agents are blocked on you", tone: "critical" }]} />
<Actions items={[{ title: "Review the ideas synthesis", why: "…", effort: "30–60 min", owner: "Alex", rec: "…" }]} />

features.title: Present mode
features.oneLiner: Press p: a title slide from the summary, then → / ← through Sections and <Step>s, ↑/↓ to scroll a tall slide, a "↓ more" hint.
features.why: Builders found the headline never appeared as a slide, revealed steps landed below the fold, and wide pages collapsed every slide to a narrow column; each was fixed in a later round.
features.how:
<Section title="Trace">
  <Step>hop 2</Step>
  <Step>hop 3</Step>
</Section>

features.title: Present steps for custom components
features.oneLiner: `usePresentSteps(n)` gives a component its own step counter that stays in sync with → / Space and with clicks.
features.why: The Collie UI explainer counted hidden step markers with a MutationObserver; the investigation page needed 5 empty <Step>s and then drifted out of sync after a click.
features.how:
const { step, setStep, active, markers } = usePresentSteps(5);
return <>{markers}<Panel i={step} onPick={setStep} /></>;

features.title: Compact header, sources behind one button
features.oneLiner: Title, summary and an as-of time; header sources collapse into "Sources (n)".
features.why: With 8–10 sources the header pushed the first decision below the fold on three demo pages.
features.how:
// artifact.json
{ "title": "…", "summary": "…", "asOf": "2026-10-12T13:45:00Z", "timeZone": "Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh", "sources": [ … ] }

features.title: Quiet folding and <More>
features.oneLiner: Click any section heading to fold it; authors put skippable detail in `<More label>`; Fold all / Unfold all sit in the ? panel.
features.why: Replaces Detail 1–4 (see removed). Alex: zoom levels take a lot of attention and don't deserve it.
features.how: <More label="Method">…</More>

features.title: Download the same single file
features.oneLiner: A Download button in the host bar saves the page as one self-contained HTML file.
features.why: Sharing is a single HTML file for now (decision Oct 11); the reader should be able to pass it on from the page itself.
features.how: // on by default; artifact.json { "host": { "download": false } } hides it

features.title: Gallery: tiles with drill-down, variants, lightbox
features.oneLiner: Tiles with thumb, status and badges; click one and its detail opens below. Or one variant at a time with an aside. Images open in a lightbox.
features.why: A run recap of 16 branches is a gallery with drill-down; the canvas-run builder wrote ~80 lines for it and the Collie UI builder wrote its own theme switcher. Both ported to <Gallery>.
features.how: <Gallery layout="tiles" items={demos.map((d) => ({ label: d.title, thumb: d.shot, status: d.verdict, badges: [d.kind], detail: <Detail d={d} /> }))} />

features.title: Decision walk: answer on the page
features.oneLiner: Readers answer each <Decision> (an option, their own, or "not sure / discuss", plus a note); <When> shows follow-ups by answer; present mode ends on a summary slide.
features.why: Alex (Oct 12): interactive decisions, an async "grill me" for a batch of decisions when the reader is away from chat.
features.how:
<DecisionIndex />
<Decision id="d1" question="Start idea 11?" options={[{ label: "Go, after merge steps 1–3" }, { label: "Not now" }]} recommend={0} owner="Alex" why="…" />
<When decision="d1" is="a">…follow-up Decision…</When>

Decision.question: Which experience should become the kit's layout?

options.label: Scrollytelling with a sticky live demo

features.title: One Feedback drawer
features.oneLiner: Decisions (with progress, "2/5 decided") and comments on any element in one drawer; Copy decisions or Copy all feedback gives Markdown with element ids for the agent.
features.why: Alex (Oct 12): one drawer to list, add and copy feedback; stored in the browser for now behind a storage interface, persisted by a hosted server later.
features.how: // host feature: press c to comment on any element; the drawer's Copy all feedback → paste back to the agent

features.title: Scorecard and RiskMatrix
features.oneLiner: Options × weighted criteria with a grade per cell and a recommended column; likelihood × impact grid with chips that link to the mitigation table.
features.why: The canvas proposal builder wrote both by hand (~60 lines); the audit counted ~25 "compare X vs Y" asks. Porting the proposal removed 131 lines.
features.how: <Scorecard options={["Electron 44", "Tauri v2"]} rows={[{ name: "Capture code", weight: "med", cells: [{ grade: "best", text: "capturePage, built in" }, { grade: "weak", text: "~150 lines objc2, macOS only" }] }]} recommend={0} />

features.title: Map fits its column
features.oneLiner: Grouped node graph that fits width and height, with Fit / 100% / zoom / drag, click-to-focus notes and nodes that link to sections.
features.why: In the first demos the map scrolled sideways or clipped the plan's goal nodes; check now warns when the fit scale drops under 65%.
features.how: <Map nodes={[{ id: "m3", label: "Merge steps 1–3", group: "core", state: "risk", note: "…" }]} edges={[{ from: "m3", to: "merge" }]} groups={[{ id: "core", label: "Core" }]} />

features.title: Code and diffs with notes
features.oneLiner: <Diff> picks hunks from a real patch; <Code> shows line ranges with "N lines hidden" gaps; both take notes keyed by line or by matching text, plus wrap and a repo path/link.
features.why: Prefer real evidence over describing it. The Collie UI trace wanted per-line "why" notes; the investigation page had to grep line numbers, so notes can now match text.
features.how:
<Diff patch="evidence/actor.patch" file="src/core/store.ts" hunks="1" notes={{ "actor": "one line in dispatch" }} />
<Code file="evidence/semantic.tokens.json" ranges="36-38,45-57" highlight="49-52" notes={{ 50: "step 9 = solid fill, in every hue" }} />

features.title: TimeAxis: a real time scale
features.oneLiner: Events, ranges, bands and lanes on a real axis; segments break it (6 weeks, then 36 hours) and say so.
features.why: The investigation page covered weeks of releases and then hours of impact; the builder hand-drew an SVG. Then Alex didn't understand the one timeline carrying two scales, which became the guide rule "one claim per picture".
features.how: <TimeAxis title="…" events={[{ at: "2026-10-12T20:01:00+07:00", label: "round 1" }]} segments={[{ from, to, weight: 1 }, { from, to, weight: 2 }]} />

TimeAxis.title: Thirteen rounds, Oct 12–13
TimeAxis.lead: First commit of each round on the kit branch (+07).

features.title: Timeline swimlanes that pack
features.oneLiner: Timeline items in lanes (you / agents / lead); same `when` shares a row; `bucket` and `compact` keep it short.
features.why: One row per event made 12 events in 3 lanes ~1300 px tall; the canvas-run builder fell back to a table. The multi-page run recap uses the packed timeline.
features.how: <Timeline compact items={[{ when: "Oct 11 03:13", lane: "you", title: "Explore plugins + diagramming" }, { when: "Oct 11 03:13", lane: "agents", title: "Round 1 until 08:18" }]} />

features.title: Walkthrough: one case, step by step
features.oneLiner: Scenarios as tabs, steps on the left, each step's visual and text on the right, an optional state rail; every step is a present step.
features.why: Alex liked the "one order, step by step" section of an investigation page (scenario tabs × steps, state rail, mock row), which the builder had written by hand.
features.how: <Walkthrough states={["draft", "checked", "built"]} scenarios={[{ label: "One artifact", steps: [{ title: "Write index.tsx", state: "draft", body: "…" }] }]} />

steps.title: Write the page
steps.body: index.tsx with kit components; data in data/, proof in evidence/.

steps.title: check until ok
steps.body: Bundle, types, render, evidence, size, plus taste advice.

steps.title: shot and look
steps.body: PNGs in both themes and every present step; fix what looks wrong.

steps.title: build one file
steps.body: Everything inlined into one HTML file.

steps.title: Answer and copy back
steps.body: Decide, comment, Copy all feedback; one paste back to the agent.

features.title: Stages: compare a few states row by row
features.oneLiner: Columns are stages, rows are the same questions asked of each, cells take a tone.
features.why: Splitting the investigation timeline needed a small "what changed per release" strip; Stages replaced the custom one 1:1.
features.how: <Stages stages={[{ title: "Round 1" }, { title: "Round 13" }]} rows={[{ label: "tests", cells: ["88", "128"] }]} />

features.title: artifact new | dev | check | build
features.oneLiner: Scaffold, live reload on loopback, check (bundle, types, render, evidence, size), and build to one self-contained HTML.
features.why: Sharing is a single HTML file for now (decision Oct 11); agents need a tight write → check → build loop.
features.how:
artifact new notes/status-1012 --kind status
artifact dev notes/status-1012.artifact
artifact check notes/status-1012.artifact
artifact build notes/status-1012.artifact -o status.html

features.title: Evidence stays inside evidence/
features.oneLiner: Evidence paths can't use `..` or symlinks out of the artifact; dev answers only known Host headers.
features.why: The first kit review (verdict: changes) found a high-severity hole: a cited path like `evidence/../../secret.txt` got inlined into the shareable HTML.
features.how: <Code file="evidence/../../secret.txt" />   // check: evidence paths must stay inside evidence/

features.title: artifact shot: agents look at their own page
features.oneLiner: PNGs of the built page in both themes, every present step, per page, or split into screen-tall pieces.
features.why: Builders borrowed playwright from other worktrees to check their pages; one had to crop a 1280×5720 shot on a VM with no image tools.
features.how:
artifact shot x.artifact --theme both --present all
artifact shot x.artifact --page all --split --height 800

features.title: artifact capture: screenshots of running apps
features.oneLiner: Headless screenshot of a URL or built file into evidence/, with selector, wait, theme and click/type steps; JPEG is ~4× smaller.
features.why: Only 4 of 16 canvas branches had a screenshot; the canvas-run builder wrote the same playwright loop three times to capture 8 more.
features.how: artifact capture http://127.0.0.1:5211 -o x.artifact/evidence/app.jpg --selector main --wait 800 --steps steps.json

features.title: artifact gather: collectors into data/
features.oneLiner: gh-prs, board and git-log collectors write data/<kind>.json; --fields / --count trim it; git-log --branches counts unique commits.
features.why: The status builder wrote its own gather.sh, and summing per-branch counts reported 278 commits where the real unique number was 150.
features.how:
artifact gather gh-prs x.artifact --repos owner/a,owner/b --since 2026-10-11
artifact gather git-log x.artifact --repo ~/code/canvas --branches 'idea/*' --base poc

features.title: check gives taste advice
features.oneLiner: Warnings that steer without templates: long pages, 20+ row tables outside <More>, a map fitted under 65%, grouped maps with back-edges, cited commits on no remote.
features.why: The reader review found every demo too long, three repeating their summary in a Callout, and a dead commit link a teammate would hit.
features.how: artifact check x.artifact   # errors fail; advice is printed as warnings

features.title: Multi-page artifacts
features.oneLiner: pages/<id>.tsx become hash routes in the same single HTML: grouped left nav with each page's sections, Previous / Next, <PageCards> on home, <Link to="id#section">; comments and decisions work across pages.
features.why: Alex (Oct 13): one long page of sections isn't great organization. The canvas run recap went from one 8.9k px page to pages of at most ~2.8k px.

features.title: Tour across pages
features.oneLiner: `"tour": ["home", "round-1", …]` in artifact.json adds a Tour button that presents those pages in order; Present on its own presents the current page.
features.why: Present mode walked one page; a multi-page recap needs one walk across its pages in the author's order.
features.how:
// artifact.json
{ "tour": ["home", "round-1", "round-2", "oct-12", "merge-plan", "findings"] }

removed.title: Detail 1–4 (zoom levels) and depth
removed.oneLiner: The reader's Detail 1–4 control (keys 1–4 zoomed the outline: sections collapse, heavy blocks stub) and `<Depth level>` / artifact.json `depth` are gone. `<Depth>` stays as a deprecated alias of `<More>`.
removed.why: Alex (Oct 12): it takes a lot of attention and doesn't deserve it. It reverses the Oct 9 decision to number zoom levels 1–4; replaced by quiet folding per section and author <More> disclosures.

removed.title: The recap POC's fixed format
removed.oneLiner: Fixed kinds, the zoom ladder and a fixed block list from the recap POC (task-1) are not part of the kit.
removed.why: Alex (Oct 12): too structured. Tool only; the agent picks the structure and kind is a free label.
